_meta.description: Golden query set for benchmark_precision_snapshot.py / compare_benchmark_runs.py -- a before/after precision-and-latency regression harness for search_memory(), run against a throwaway copy of the live SALTMDB corpus (never ~/.saltmdb/saltmdb.db itself). Distinct from scripts/benchmarking/benchmark_rerank_gap_gate.py's QUERIES list (which measures raw RRF-fusion score ratios for gap-gate threshold calibration) -- this set measures end-to-end search_memory() ranking correctness across code changes, not a single internal ratio.
_meta.provenance: Each query is real and hand-picked against known live-corpus content as of 2026-08-06 (not synthetic). expected_entity_id is the entity that should rank first (or within top_k for ambiguous/near-duplicate cases) as judged by a human/agent reading the actual memory content at curation time -- there is no ground-truth oracle table in SALTMDB, so this file IS the oracle. Two entries (chunk-embed-backfill-timing, dismiss-event-mixed-type-bug) are the same two fixed regression anchors used in benchmark_rerank_gap_gate.py's QUERIES (021eb8ee's original 12-query battery Q1/Q8).

category_meanings.decisive: Clean, specific phrasing with one clearly-correct answer -- expected to rank 1st regardless of ranking-flag settings. A regression here means something broke, not a legitimate ranking trade-off.
category_meanings.ambiguous_near_duplicate: A correction/near-duplicate pair exists on the same narrow topic (e.g. a bug-fix memo and a later correction memo about a related but distinct claim). top_k tolerance is 2 instead of 1 -- these are exactly the cases where rerank_by_topic/demote_superseded can legitimately swap ordering without it being a real precision loss, per 021eb8ee's finding.

_meta.maintenance_note: Entries reference real entity IDs -- if a referenced memory is ever archived/superseded/consolidated away, its query stops being meaningful and should be re-pointed at the successor or retired. Re-verify expected_entity_id still resolves before trusting a comparison run.
_meta.held_out_meaning: 4 entries carry "held_out": true. All entries here were sanity-checked once against real search_memory() output at curation time (that pass is what caught 5 initially-mislabeled 'decisive' entries below and reclassified them). The held_out/primary split is about what happens AFTER curation: if RERANK_GAP_SKIP_RATIO or any other threshold/config value is ever re-tuned in the future, only the primary set should inform that decision -- held_out entries are reported (and still count toward compare_benchmark_runs.py's regression exit code) but must never be the thing a threshold gets adjusted to satisfy, or this file stops being an independent check and becomes circular.
